summary: A bipolar transistor lets a microcontroller pin switch a load that needs far more current than the pin can give. You learn the three regions, size a base resistor so a relay switches fully on, and see why a transistor left in the active region gets hot.
html:
How an NPN transistor switches

An NPN BJT has three terminals: base, collector and emitter. A small base current IB​ (into the base, out of the emitter) allows a much larger collector current:

  • Cut-off: $V_{BE} < $ about 0.6 V and no base current, so the transistor is off and IC​≈0.
  • Active: IC​=βIB​, with β (also called hFE​) typically 50 to 400. It varies widely between parts and with temperature and current, so never design for an exact value. VCE​ is whatever the rest of the circuit leaves.
  • Saturation: the load limits the current below βIB​. The transistor is fully on with VCE(sat)​≈0.1–0.3 V.

As a switch, you want only cut-off and saturation. Dissipation is VCE​IC​: near zero in both of those states, but large in the active region where both are significant.

The low-side switch. The load goes from the supply to the collector, the emitter goes to ground, and the GPIO pin drives the base through a resistor RB​:

IB​=RB​Vin​−VBE​​,saturated if βmin​IB​>IC(sat)​=Rload​VCC​−VCE(sat)​​.

Design with an overdrive factor of 2 to 5 over the minimum β so the switch saturates for every part and temperature. Add a flyback diode across inductive loads (lesson 6).

Worked example

A 3.3 V pin drives a 12 V relay with a 400 Ω coil. The datasheet guarantees β≥100.

  1. Load current when fully on: (12−0.2)/400=29.5 mA, more than most GPIO pins should supply.
  2. Minimum base current: 29.5/100=0.295 mA. With an overdrive of 3: 0.885 mA.
  3. RB​=(3.3−0.7)/0.885=2.94 kΩ; use 2.7 kΩ, giving IB​=0.963 mA.
  4. With 4.7 kΩ: IB​=0.553 mA and βIB​=55.3 mA > 29.5 mA, so it still saturates (overdrive 1.9) and dissipates 0.2×29.5=5.9 mW.
  5. With 47 kΩ: IB​=55.3 µA and IC​=5.5 mA, active region. VCE​=12−5.53×0.4=9.79 V, dissipation 54 mW, and the relay never pulls in.

Code it from scratch

bjt_switch.py
VBE, VCESAT = 0.7, 0.2

def switch(vin, rb, beta, vcc, rload):
    """Piecewise model of an NPN low-side switch. Returns (region, ib, ic, vce, power)."""
    ib = max(0.0, (vin - VBE) / rb)
    ic_sat = (vcc - VCESAT) / rload
    if ib == 0:
        return "cutoff", 0.0, 0.0, vcc, 0.0
    if beta * ib >= ic_sat:
        return "saturation", ib, ic_sat, VCESAT, VCESAT * ic_sat
    ic = beta * ib
    vce = vcc - ic * rload
    return "active", ib, ic, vce, vce * ic

def base_resistor(vin, ic, beta_min, overdrive=3.0):
    return (vin - VBE) / (overdrive * ic / beta_min)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    ic = (12 - VCESAT) / 400
    assert abs(ic - 0.0295) < 1e-12
    rb = base_resistor(3.3, ic, 100)
    assert abs(rb - 2937.9) < 0.1
    for beta in (100, 150, 400):                     # every guaranteed part saturates with 2.7 k
        assert switch(3.3, 2700, beta, 12, 400)[0] == "saturation"
    reg, ib, ic2, vce, p = switch(3.3, 4700, 100, 12, 400)
    assert reg == "saturation" and abs(p - 0.0059) < 1e-6 and abs(100 * ib / ic2 - 1.8745) < 1e-3
    reg, ib, ic3, vce, p = switch(3.3, 47000, 100, 12, 400)
    print(f"47 k base resistor: {reg}, Ic = {ic3*1e3:.2f} mA, Vce = {vce:.2f} V, P = {p*1e3:.1f} mW")
    assert reg == "active" and abs(vce - 9.787) < 1e-3 and abs(p - 0.05412) < 1e-4
    assert switch(0.0, 2700, 100, 12, 400)[0] == "cutoff"

Exercises

A BJT with βmin​=50 must switch a 1 A load from a 5 V pin with overdrive 2. What base current and resistor do you need, and is that reasonable?

Show the solution

IB​=2×1/50=40 mA and RB​=4.3/0.04=107.5 Ω. 40 mA is too much for a GPIO pin. Use a logic-level MOSFET (lesson 13) or a Darlington pair instead.

Where is the transistor’s dissipation highest as Vin​ ramps slowly from 0 to 3.3 V with the relay load?

Show the solution

In the active region P=(VCC​−IC​R)IC​, which peaks when IC​R=VCC​/2: IC​=15 mA and P=6×0.015=90 mW. Switch quickly through this region.

Quiz

quiz.q: Relay current in mA when the switch is fully on (12 V, 400 Ω, VCE(sat) 0.2 V)?
quiz.explain: (VCC​−VCE(sat)​)/R.

quiz.q: Base resistor in kΩ for overdrive 3 with βmin = 100 from a 3.3 V pin?
quiz.explain: IB​=3IC​/βmin​.

quiz.q: A BJT used as a switch should operate in…
With a 47 kΩ base resistor and β = 100, what is VCE in volts?
What is the maximum active-region dissipation in mW for 12 V and 400 Ω?
quiz.explain: VCC2​/(4R) at half the supply.

quiz.q: Why design with overdrive instead of exactly IB​=IC​/β?
quiz.explain: The guaranteed minimum β must still saturate.
options: it makes the transistor slower on purpose
